[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The IRSA service account can be created before its namespace, since both use the same variable but the service account does not reference the namespace resource. Order the service account after the namespace to avoid Kubernetes rejecting creation when this instance creates the namespace.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When this IRSA module creates its namespace, the ServiceAccount still uses only the namespace input string and does not wait for that namespace resource. Kubernetes can reject ServiceAccount creation if the namespace is not yet present.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The KEDA IRSA service account uses a literal namespace input while this module also creates that namespace, so Terraform may try to create the service account first. Reference the created namespace to establish the required ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The KEDA IRSA ServiceAccount is configured with a module-created namespace, but its namespace attribute is only the input string. Add a dependency on the namespace resource to prevent creation before that namespace exists.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The deployment names the aws-otel-eks namespace with a literal rather than referencing the namespace resource, allowing the deployment to be applied before the namespace exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Kubernetes Deployment uses the fixed aws-otel-eks namespace name and has no dependency on the namespace resource, so Terraform may create it before the namespace exists. Reference the namespace resource to enforce creation order.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar` places its pods in namespace `aws-otel-eks` using a hard-coded local string instead of a reference to `kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks`, so Terraform may attempt to create the deployment before the namespace exists and the apply fails with "namespaces \"aws-otel-eks\" not found".

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.kubernetes-addons.module.aws_opentelemetry_collector:resource.kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar sets metadata.namespace from the local string local.default_addon_config["namespace"] instead of referencing kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks, so there is no ordering between them and the deployment is applied before the namespace exists on a fresh cluster. Add an explicit dependency (or reference the namespace resource) so the deployment is created after the namespace.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The load balancer controller Helm release waits for its IAM role and service account, but not for the policy attachment that grants the role its controller permissions. The chart can be installed before those permissions are effective.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The load-balancer controller Helm release waits for its IAM role and service account, but not the policy attachment granting that role controller permissions. The workload could start before those permissions are attached.
